ops.statement: Use python -m <tool> rather than bare <tool> in command postconditions
ops.title: Prefer python -m <tool> form in command postconditions
ops.body:
When authoring command postconditions for Python tools (pytest, black, mypy, etc.), use `python -m <tool>` rather than bare `<tool>` to avoid PATH availability issues across environments.

**Why**: Command postconditions run under the engine's POSIX shell, where tool executables may not be in PATH even when `python -m <tool>` works. This manifests as exit code 127 (command not found) forcing manual verification and human waivers.

**How to apply**: In execute.json gate postconditions, write `python -m pytest` not `pytest`, `python -m black` not `black`, etc.

**Grounding**: euler-001-20260710 g1-integrate c1 waived (evidence e-g1-integrate-5) after `pytest` command failed with exit 127 in POSIX shell (evidence e-g1-integrate-1, e-g1-integrate-3), while manual `python -m pytest` succeeded.
